page: Microsoft Azure E104is_v5 is a memory-optimized, hardware-isolated virtual machine designed for high-density compute and in-memory operations. It runs on Microsoft Hyper-V and is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The server exposes 104 vCPUs derived from 52 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Compute capabilities are bolstered by hardware instructions including AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 672.0 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 6.46 GB per vCPU. It features no local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel performance and strong memory throughput. The instance ranks in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core execution (100,847.42) and Geekbench multi-core throughput (17,614.0), alongside top 10% PassMark encryption results (91,285.35). Memory benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 308.31 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 120.44 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance achieved 90.58 million operations/sec on Redis SET benchmarks and a PassMark database score of 30,031.01. Single-core performance, such as Geekbench single-core (1,695.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,899.78), stays in the average range.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, the E104is_v5 delivers high resource density and isolation on dedicated physical hardware. However, lack of local ephemeral disk space requires remote attached storage for stateful workloads. Hardware acceleration for AI generation is constrained by the absence of dedicated GPUs, reflected in weak large-model LLM generation speeds (2.65 tokens/sec). The server is ideally suited for massive in-memory databases, enterprise relational database servers, distributed cache layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E104is_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance featuring 104 vCPUs across 52 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 672.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local disk storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate upper-quartile multi-core capabilities, registering a multi-core stress-ng score of 100,847.42, alongside high memory bandwidth with 308.31 GB/sec uncached reads and 120.44 GB/sec uncached writes. Database handling is robust, reaching 90.58 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and top-tier PassMark encryption performance. While single-threaded speeds and CPU-based large language model generation remain average to weak, the high memory density and dedicated hardware footprint make it well suited for large in-memory caching layers, relational database engines, and demanding parallel data processing pipelines.
